text:
**Yes, but only some models can, and a basic one may cut your computer off during an outage.**

**What to check**
- **Documented UPS/EPS mode with automatic switchover.** Anker says a basic power station may keep appliances running but still interrupt a computer or NAS during an outage ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).
- **Transfer time.** EcoFlow says many products advertised as UPS take 20-30 ms or more to switch, which it considers too slow for desktops and hard drives. It says "9 times out of 10" a power station isn't a true UPS, though that comes from a manufacturer's blog ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)).
- **Pure sine wave output.** Anker recommends it for computers, monitors and networking gear.
- **Pass-through support.** The unit must be able to run continuously while plugged into the wall.
- **Enough wattage and battery.** Add up your computer's real draw and compare it to the station's continuous output. Runtime is roughly Wh × 0.85 ÷ watts.

**Limits**
- A 10 ms switchover is fast, but it isn't the 0 ms of an online double-conversion UPS ([Anker's NAS guide](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)). Check your PC power supply's manual. If it requires 0 ms or continuous voltage regulation, buy an online UPS instead.
- A power station is not a replacement for a UPS in critical or server setups.

**Models that publish UPS specs in these results**
- **Anker SOLIX S2000** has a 10 ms UPS switchover, 2,010 Wh, and 1,500 W pure sine wave output. It was listed at $699.99 after coupon. I don't have a direct product-page link, but the Shop Now button is on [Anker's article](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups).
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** has a switchover under 10 ms and 600 W AC output, which EcoFlow says is plenty for a desktop plus external drives. The product link is in [EcoFlow's article](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply), but I don't have a price.

The BLUETTI and ALLPOWERS units on the Dealectric coupon page don't list UPS specs in these results, so I can't say they work as a UPS. Check each model's manual before buying.

If you tell me your computer's wattage and how many minutes of backup you want, I can estimate the battery size you need.
